bullets.title: Fed expected to hike 25bps Wednesday; two hikes total in 2026, then pause
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley expects 25bp hikes in September and December, with the SEP median projecting two 2026 hikes followed by one cut each in 2027 and 2028. Piper Sandler's macro team concurs, forecasting zero dissents at Wednesday's FOMC with a median SEP rate of 4.1% for 2026. Sticky inflation, second-round energy price effects, and AI-driven investment demand are cited as the rationale for continued tightening, with MS recommending neutral duration on US Treasuries.

bullets.title: 10Y yield touched 5% for first time in 3 years before retreating; real yield breaking out
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury briefly touched 5% intraday before pulling back; real 10-year yields have broken out of a 3-year base (1.5%-2.5% range) with a technical target of 3.5%. JPMorgan's Treasury survey shows clients at their longest positioning in 10 months, with potential position squaring seen as a headwind; next technical support is 4.12-4.22%. US Treasuries outperformed DM peers on the day, partly on Trump's Russia-Ukraine de-escalation announcement.

bullets.title: US equities ended lower but well off session lows; Nasdaq -0.56%, S&P -0.48%
bullets.body: The primary driver was rotation out of AI infrastructure stocks following Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to slow frontier model development citing recursive self-improvement and rogue agent risks. Semis led the selloff (SOX -5.9%) while software (+3.2%), IT services (+4.0%), and comm services (+2.8%) outperformed as AI slowdown talk eased disintermediation fears. S&P futures recovered to +0.09% after hours at ~7,700.

bullets.title: Anthropic AI pacing call sparks sharp AI infrastructure selloff; analysts skeptical slowdown materializes
bullets.body: Anthropic CEO called for slowing frontier AI development; NVDA fell 3.4-4.1%, AMD -6.3%, MRVL -9.0%, AVGO -4.1%, ORCL -5.6% on the day. Analysts broadly view voluntary AI pacing as unlikely without global coordination, particularly Chinese participation, given US competitive and geopolitical pressure. Wells Fargo notes physical permitting and power constraints—not policy—are more likely to extend the capex cycle, and sees data center REIT weakness as overdone.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO viewed as key 2026 AI trade re-ignition catalyst; NVDA in talks for $10B anchor stake
bullets.body: NVDA is reportedly in talks to invest up to $10B in Anthropic's upcoming IPO, and Anthropic is said to be profitable for a second straight quarter with gross margins >80%. OpenAI CEO Altman confirmed no IPO in 2026 (now expected 2027). One view holds the Anthropic IPO is the critical catalyst to reconnect AI stocks with underlying infrastructure demand fundamentals from NVDA, AVGO, and DELL.

bullets.title: Microsoft tightens AI safety controls; Anthropic restricted at NVDA, PLTR, Booz Allen over data security
bullets.body: Microsoft posted a new AI code of conduct requiring human control and barring models from resisting shutdown. Anthropic faces model-use restrictions at Nvidia, Palantir, and Booz Allen Hamilton over data security concerns. These developments are compounding near-term sentiment headwinds for AI infrastructure names.

bullets.title: Oil spikes on Middle East escalation; WTI +1.3% to $101, Saudi pipeline offline ~1 month
bullets.body: WTI rose 1.3% to $101.39 and Brent +1.0% to $105.68 after Houthi drone strikes took the Saudi East-West pipeline offline for ~1 month; Saudi Red Sea exports could halt within 3-5 days as Yanbu stockpiles deplete. Houthis also claimed interception of two Saudi fighter jets and captured additional Bab al-Mandib positions. Kalshi prediction markets show >70% probability US gasoline prices exceed $4.56/gallon in 2026.

bullets.title: Natural gas +2.3%; US data centers forecast to consume up to 15 Bcfd by 2035
bullets.body: Natural gas futures rose 2.3% to $2.896 with LNG feedgas flows testing 4-month highs at 18.70 Bcf. BNEF projects US data centers alone could consume up to 15 Bcfd of natural gas by 2035—topping the demand of most countries. Moody's separately estimates the US AI boom requires $110B for 45 GW of new power generation through 2030. The EPA repealed Biden-era carbon emission limits on coal- and gas-fired power plants.

bullets.title: Tightening cycle mostly priced but financial conditions remain biased tighter; AI goods/services favored over cyclicals
bullets.body: One strategist argues much of the hawkish Fed outcome is already priced, with the consumer remaining strong and only a benign slowdown—not recession—expected. In this environment, AI goods and AI services are seen as favorably positioned while cyclicals face headwinds. Piper Sandler's breadth indicators are deteriorating: the 26-week new highs signal flipped to sell, with stocks in downtrends outnumbering uptrends and SPX technical support at 7,580.

bullets.title: Memory markets tightening: DRAM +58-63%, NAND +55-60%; HBM grey-market prices multiples of global levels
bullets.body: US export controls on China AI chips have caused Chinese HBM prices to reach several times global market levels. Apple's A20 Pro launch coincides with sharp contract price increases (DRAM +58-63%, NAND +55-60%). Taiwan AI server/supply-chain revenue hit a cycle high of NT$2.84T in August (+76.5% y/y), and DDR5 RDIMM 32GB modules surged +18.8% m/m to $1,900.

bullets.title: Household deleveraging has ended; current expansion has more solid demand fundamentals than 1990s/2000s cycles
bullets.body: Household sector deleveraging appears to have ended as of Q2 2026, with the domestic private sector balance not dangerously depressed. The current expansion is underpinned by stronger demand fundamentals than the 1990s tech/telecom or 2000s housing bubbles, though the federal deficit is now much larger. The wealth effect remains strong, and the personal saving rate is not depressed relative to household net worth levels.

bullets.title: JPMorgan forecasts US headline CPI at 3.4-3.7% through Oct 2026; PCE at 3.7-3.9%
bullets.body: JPMorgan's monthly inflation forecast shows US headline CPI stable at 3.4% July-September before rising to 3.7% in October 2026. US PCE inflation is projected at 3.7-3.9% over the same period. Core CPI in major DM economies remains stable to rising modestly, consistent with the continued tightening bias at the Fed.

bullets.title: Capex broadening beyond AI into industrials; UBS argues non-AI industrials offer better upside
bullets.body: UBS strategists argue that as capex broadens beyond AI to other industrial sectors, the most compelling opportunities may now be in industrial companies that have barely benefited from the AI boom. Piper Sandler similarly expects conventional factory capex to pick up in 2027, aided by OBBA full-capex expensing which cut corporate cash tax rates by ~5.4 percentage points.

bullets.title: Agentic commerce: <0.2% of e-commerce visits today, but winners being decided now via infrastructure readiness
bullets.body: Hedgeye estimates AI agents currently drive ~1 visit per 600 total e-commerce visits and adoption hasn't accelerated since April 2026, but argues winners are being selected now based on MCP server readiness, LLMs.txt compliance, and inventory access. The long-term opportunity is modeled at ~$329B annually. Retail media is flagged as the most exposed high-margin profit pool, and mid-tier undifferentiated brands face the sharpest structural risk.

bullets.title: Steeper yield curve is a tailwind for midcap banks; Morgan Stanley upgrades M&T, initiates Pinnacle at OW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded M&T Bank to Overweight as its top midcap bank pick and initiated Pinnacle Financial at Overweight, arguing a steeper yield curve benefits rather than pressures midcap banks with strong operating account relationships. First Horizon was initiated at Equal-weight.

bullets.title: US private credit default rates hit record 6.3%; BofA CEO expects flat Q3 trading revenue
bullets.body: US private credit default rates reached a record 6.3%, adding to concerns around tighter financial conditions. BofA CEO Moynihan separately indicated trading revenue would be relatively flat versus Q3 last year. The Fed pause risks further US bond market turmoil via credibility concerns, per one analyst.

bullets.title: Midterm election scenarios and fiscal policy implications flagged as pre-November positioning focus
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley is hosting a September 18th cross-asset webcast on US midterm election outcomes and their implications for fiscal policy, US growth, the dollar, and broader asset class positioning. Markets are seen as partially but not fully pricing different fiscal scenarios into November.

bullets.title: AI security spending shifting from visibility tools to runtime trust and identity governance
bullets.body: CISO feedback from a security partner call shows AI security spending is becoming more disciplined and ROI-focused, with priorities shifting from inventory/visibility toward runtime trust, authorization, and non-human identity (NHI) management. AI agents are increasingly treated as digital workers requiring identity governance, onboarding, and entitlement controls. SASE vendors face convergence risk as architectures homogenize.

bullets.title: Data center REITs sold off sharply on AI pacing fears; analysts see fundamentals as intact in Sunbelt
bullets.body: Data center REITs fell ~4.26% on the day (DLR ~5%, EQIX -3.8%) on Anthropic's AI slowdown call, with HPC names HUT and WULF also declining sharply. Analysts view the selloff as overdone, noting Sunbelt data center fundamentals remain steady while West Coast lab space faces more genuine pressure. IREN was upgraded to Overweight at JPMorgan with a $65 target.

bullets.title: Piper macro: nominal GDP on track for 7%+ growth; multiple stimulative policies point to sticky inflation
bullets.body: Piper Sandler's macro team sees eco tailwinds (M2 growth, bank loan expansion, OBBA capex expensing) vastly exceeding headwinds, with nominal growth poised to exceed 7% and the 10Y yield directionally fair near 5%. Multiple stimulative policies—fiscal, monetary easing of lending standards—point to persistent inflation, consistent with the continued Fed tightening bias through early 2027.
